newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola to shortly name deep water operators.
newsitem.headline: Angola to shortly name deep water operators.

text.p: The Angolan government is likely to award operator licences to oil companies in three deep water blocks by the end of February with bids opening on three more soon afterwards, an Angolan oil analyst said on Monday.
"We should know by the end of the month who the operators will be in blocks 19, 21 and 22," said Jose de Oliveira, who also edits the monthly Energia magazine.
"As soon as the operators are awarded for those blocks, the government will start taking bids on blocks 23, 24 and 25," he added.

World Bank statistics show Angolan oil production is worth nearly $4 billion annually. After Nigeria, Angola is the second largest oil producer in sub-Saharan Africa with a projected 760,000 barrels a day in 1996, up from 560,000 in 1995.
Production is expected to rise considerably as the government begins to hand out the first deep water concessions west and Southwest of the capital Luanda.
Until now, the government has issued deep water blocks just around the northern enclave of Cabinda.
French oil company Elf Aquitaine struck water in 1,365 metres in the northern block 17 last year.
Although the extent of the Elf find is not yet known, initial studies are encouraging.
"Of course there is a lot of speculation about which block is the best, but the seismic data for block 22 is particularly encouraging and the companies really fought for that one," Oliveira said.
He said there was also evidence of oil on block 22.

"Mobil Oil Corp l has also made a very interesting discovery on block 20. That block is not commercial but it looks as though they have found a very good oil structure there that points toward a larger amount of oil farther to the south in block 22," he said.
Seismic data on block 25 has also shown potential, he said.
U.S-based Texaco Inc, Broken Hill Properties and Brazil's Petrobras have bid for blocks 19, 21 and 22.
